card.name: Verb 'occur' after may or can
card.fires_on: The verb 'occur' (or 'been') right after a modal such as 'can also', 'may' or 'has', where a warning says an adverse event happens. It is common in warning sections about serotonin syndrome, hyponatremia and similar effects.

modes.label: occur after modal
modes.description: The word 'occur' follows 'can also' or 'may' in a warning about an adverse effect.
modes.example: Serotonin syndrome can also<< occur>> when these drugs are used alone.

modes.label: been after has
modes.example: although oligohydramnios has<< been>> infrequently reported as soon as 4

card.writes: It adds little clear output; the promoted and suppressed tokens are mostly Chinese words about events and disasters.
card.plain: It marks the verb 'occur' in phrases saying a side effect may happen.
